The attention data shows that there are abnormal peaks in some quarters. Combined with the increasing number of infections year by year, this can maximize the efficiency of resources and enhance the prevention awareness.
answer.C: Increase the investment in publicity resources for all age groups and all knowledge areas because improving the overall public awareness is the foundation for disease prevention.
answer.D: Increase special education content for key prevention areas with low attention (such as symptom recognition and incubation period information). Although the attention to knowledge such as transmission routes is relatively high, the attention to other areas is insufficient. Combined with the infection trend, strengthening these weak links can reduce knowledge blind spots and lower the risk of transmission.
answer.E: Concentrate the resources during the quarters with the lowest attention (such as the third quarter of 2015) because the public is more likely to accept new information during the trough of attention.
answer.F: Give priority to strengthening the education on transmission routes (with 95% attention) and ignore other knowledge areas because high attention indicates that this area is the most effective.
